channel.who: Your players, then the tournament director if a rule is unclear
channel.how: Talk to the team at the next practice; take any rule question to the director calmly between innings, never a judgment call.

output.teachable_moment: Winning comes from a winning formula: Winning is fun and feels great, but it doesn't happen without a winning formula: healthy arms, many players who can contribute, and everyone playing their part. Don't put the scoreboard above developing players.

individual: Track pitches every outing and plan the rotation before a tournament weekend.
team: Between-outing recovery circuit: Light movement, band work, and a short catch progression the day after a high-pitch outing. Stop at any sharp elbow or shoulder pain and check rest rules before the next live inning. Safety: This is recovery, not a bullpen. No max-effort throws. Pair with the pitcher’s remaining rest days.
at_home: Protect arms and build depth: give more pitchers reps in lower-pressure innings so they're ready when you need them. Rest your best arm when the rules or their body say so.

life_lesson.text: Long-term success comes from building people and habits, not from chasing one result at any cost.

lessons.title: Winning comes from a winning formula
lessons.principle: Winning is fun and feels great, but it doesn't happen without a winning formula: healthy arms, many players who can contribute, and everyone playing their part. Don't put the scoreboard above developing players.

lessons.title: Believe in your players before they believe in themselves
lessons.principle: Have confidence in your players even when they don't show it, even when their track record says failure. Don't lose that confidence. Feed it to them and they will succeed.
